patches.old: Under standard conditions, which of the following reactions is spontaneous based on standard reduction potentials? (E°: Fe3+/Fe2+ = +0.77 V; I2/I- = +0.54 V; Ag+/Ag = +0.80 V; Sn4+/Sn2+ = +0.15 V)
patches.new: Under standard conditions, which of the following reactions is NOT spontaneous based on standard reduction potentials? (E°: Fe3+/Fe2+ = +0.77 V; I2/I- = +0.54 V; Ag+/Ag = +0.80 V; Sn4+/Sn2+ = +0.15 V)
patches.reason: As written the item had three correct answers. I⁻ reducing Fe³⁺ gives +0.23 V, Fe²⁺ reducing Ag⁺ gives +0.03 V, and Sn²⁺ reducing I₂ gives +0.39 V — all spontaneous. Only Fe²⁺ reducing I₂ is not, at −0.23 V. Asking which is NOT spontaneous makes exactly one choice correct and keeps all four worth evaluating.
With the stem asking which reaction is not spontaneous, the answer is D: Fe²⁺ reducing I₂ requires I₂/I⁻ (+0.54 V) as the cathode against Fe³⁺/Fe²⁺ (+0.77 V) as the anode, giving E°cell = −0.23 V.

patches.old: For spontaneity, E°cell = E°cathode - E°anode must be positive. In choice A, Fe3+ is reduced (cathode, +0.77 V) and I- is oxidized (anode, +0.54 V), giving E°cell = 0.77 - 0.54 = +0.23 V, which is positive and therefore spontaneous. Choice B gives 0.80 - 0.77 = +0.03 V for Ag+ reduction, but Fe2+ oxidation is the anode; this is actually spontaneous too, but choice A is the primary correct answer. Wait, re-evaluating: choice B: E°cell = E°(Ag+/Ag) - E°(Fe3+/Fe2+) = 0.80 - 0.77 = +0.03 V, which is also spontaneous. However, choice A yields a clearly positive E°cell and is the best supported answer. Choices C and D both yield negative E°cell values, confirming nonspontaneity.
patches.new: Work out E°cell = E°cathode − E°anode for each, remembering that the species being reduced is the cathode. Choice A: Fe3+ reduced (+0.77) against I- oxidised (+0.54) gives +0.23 V, spontaneous. Choice B: Ag+ reduced (+0.80) against Fe2+ oxidised (+0.77) gives +0.03 V, spontaneous but only just. Choice C: I2 reduced (+0.54) against Sn2+ oxidised (+0.15) gives +0.39 V, spontaneous. Choice D: I2 reduced (+0.54) against Fe2+ oxidised (+0.77) gives −0.23 V, so this one is not spontaneous — which makes sense, since it is simply the reverse of choice A. A reaction and its reverse cannot both be spontaneous, and spotting that pairing answers the question without any arithmetic.
patches.reason: Rewritten for the corrected stem. The old explanation worked out that choice B was also spontaneous, said so in the published text (“Wait, re-evaluating…”), and then asserted that choices C and D both give negative potentials, which is wrong for C at +0.39 V.

patches.old: But Cu has a *higher* E° than Zn²⁺/Zn, meaning Cu is a better oxidizing agent than Zn²⁺.
patches.new: But the Cu²⁺/Cu couple has a *higher* E° than Zn²⁺/Zn, meaning Cu²⁺ is the better oxidizing agent and copper metal the weaker reducing agent.
patches.reason: Copper metal is not an oxidizing agent; the oxidizing agent in that couple is Cu²⁺. Potentials belong to couples rather than to single species, and this sentence is the one place in the lesson where the distinction decides the answer.

patches.old: For n = 2, double the n in the denominator, so the same E°cell gives log K = n × E°cell / 0.0592.
patches.new: Rearranged, log K = n × E°cell / 0.0592, so for n = 2 the same cell potential corresponds to a K that is squared relative to the n = 1 case.
patches.reason: “Double the n in the denominator” is not an instruction a reader can carry out: n is the denominator, and it is set by the reaction, not doubled by the reader. The rearranged formula says what was meant.

visual.title: E°cell, ΔG° and K are one fact in three languages
visual.alt: A triangle linking standard cell potential, standard free energy change and the equilibrium constant. The edge between potential and free energy is labelled delta G equals minus nFE cell; the edge between free energy and K is labelled delta G equals minus RT ln K; the edge between potential and K is labelled E cell equals 0.0592 over n times log K. A table below lines up the three quantities: potential above zero with free energy below zero and K above one means spontaneous as written; all three at their neutral values means equilibrium; potential below zero with free energy above zero and K below one means the reverse is spontaneous. A closing note records that cell potential is intensive while free energy is extensive and scales with n.
visual.caption: Any one of the three fixes the other two. The only thing that trips people is the minus sign in ΔG° = −nFE°cell, which is what flips the direction of every inequality.
